measures.subject: Photo identification requirement for voting
measures.ballotTitle:
Proposed Constitutional Amendment
Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly
To enact Section 5 of Article V of the Constitution of the State of Ohio
A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5.
This proposed amendment would:
• Require voters to present an approved form of government-issued photo identification in order to vote.
• Allow state law to provide for an alternative method of verifying a voter’s identity for a voter who has a sincere religious objection to being photographed and, therefore, does not possess an approved form of government-issued photo identification.
• Require that voters who do not vote in person provide an approved form of government-issued photo identification, unless the law authorizes those persons to vote by providing a signature and at least one other specified unique identifier.
• Define approved forms of government-issued photo identification as an unexpired Ohio driver license or state identification card; a United States passport or passport card; or a United States military identification card, Ohio National Guard identification card, or United States Department of Veterans Affairs identification card.
If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately.
A "YES" vote means approval of the amendment. A "NO" vote means disapproval of the amendment.
SHALL THE AMENDMENT BE APPROVED?
measures.summary: Would add a requirement to the Ohio Constitution that voters present an approved government-issued photo ID to vote, with a religious-objection alternative and a possible signature-plus-identifier option for voters who do not vote in person.

measureEffectiveNote: The certified ballot language states: 'If approved, the amendment shall take effect immediately.' This overrides the Ohio Constitution's default for amendments (effective 30 days after the election). Election day, 2026-11-03, is used as the representative date; the result is formally known only once the statewide canvass is certified, weeks later.
notes: ohiosos.gov (including the county board sites it hosts at boe.ohio.gov) returned a 'Website Maintenance' 403 page throughout research, so no state-level candidate list was read. Candidates come from county board certified lists (Hamilton 9/8, Wood 8/26, Franklin rev. 10/16, Lake 8/25, Union 7/22); all five agree on every statewide race.
U.S. Senate is a special election for the unexpired term (ending 1/3/2029) of J.D. Vance's former seat, now held by appointee Jon Husted. No regular Senate election is held in Ohio in 2026.

Greg Levy (Party for Socialism and Liberation per The Green Papers) is listed by Hamilton, Wood, Franklin and Lake as an 'Other-party candidate' (Ohio's designation for petition candidates of unrecognized parties).
Ohio Supreme Court races carry party labels on the ballot. The two seats are distinguished only by term start date (1/1/2027 and 1/2/2027).
OH-1: Libertarian nominee John Hancock withdrew; Nathan Weise was certified to fill the vacancy (Hamilton County, 9/8/2026).
OH-9: Libertarian primary winner Matthew Althaus is NOT on the ballot (absent from Wood County's certified list; Ballotpedia says 'did not make the ballot'); Wikipedia still lists him.

Districts verified against an official county list: 1, 3, 5, 8, 9, 14, 15. Districts 2, 4, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13 rely on Ballotpedia, The Green Papers and Wikipedia agreeing (Wikipedia misspells OH-11's Kirchner as 'Krichner').

Issue 3 (SJR 10, legislatively referred) is the only statewide issue on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot. The text is from the Ohio Ballot Board certified ballot language (Aug 3/4, 2026), read from Signal Ohio's copy of the SOS PDF.
Ohio polls are open 6:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m.; the whole state is on Eastern time, so 7:30 PM EST (UTC-5) = 00:30 UTC Nov 4.
unconfirmed: No candidate list from the Ohio Secretary of State itself (its site was down for maintenance); the SOS form-of-ballot Directive 2026-45 could not be read.
Districts 2, 4, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13: no official county list read; exact ballot names (e.g. 'Jen' vs 'Jennifer' Mazzuckelli, 'Mike' vs 'Michael R.' Turner, middle initials) unverified.
Ballot designation for independents Tracey Tackett (OH-4) and Sandeep Dixit (OH-13): left blank; Ohio prints either 'Nonparty candidate' or nothing, and The Green Papers lists Dixit as 'Nonparty'.
Libertarian Aidan Michael Jeffery (Auditor of State) appears on Lake County's 8/25 list but not on Hamilton's (9/8), Wood's (8/26) or Franklin's (10/16) lists; he was left out as not on the ballot.
Effective date: whether 'take effect immediately' means election day or the date the result is certified was not confirmed.
